search_method: Bounded, not exhaustive: took ALL 8,434 distinct (direct_funder, upstream_source) pairs from upstream_edges (a small local table, full scan was cheap), filtered to the 6,259 upstream_source addresses NOT themselves a known CEX address, then checked the FIRST 2,000 of those (sample, disclosed) against transfer_index for `source IN (43 CEX addrs) AND destination IN (that 2,000-address sample)` in a single indexed batch query. 33 hits found in this bounded first-2000 sample alone (0.5s runtime), strongly suggesting the full 6,259-address population would yield many more -- treated as sufficient to prove hop-distance-2 chains are real and non-trivial in volume, without needing to scan the full population for this proof-of-existence task.

hot_cold_reconstruction_test.method: The REAL 2-hop chain found above (CEX -> intermediary_2 -> intermediary_1 -> creator, using the actual addresses/signatures/amounts/block_times discovered) was loaded into an isolated fixture, with the 2 older hops migrated to a COLD segment and the newest hop kept in HOT -- exactly simulating what happens after real archival.

non_attributive_but_preserved: None of these chains are treated as proving common operational control merely because a CEX address is involved (per the CEX_INFRA_PRESERVE_LINEAGE_EXCLUDE_SOLE_ATTRIBUTION rule, already established in prior milestones) -- this artifact proves ONLY that the physical lineage evidence survives HOT/COLD tiering intact, not that CEX identity implies attribution. Attribution classification is entirely out of scope for storage-lifecycle work.
